key_insight: The thesis shows that large action spaces can be made tractable by sharing structure across actions, using Bayesian exploration for on-policy learning and regularized latent/policy-weighted objectives for off-policy learning.
engineering_relevance: These methods are relevant for recommender systems, ranking, and interactive decision-making pipelines where action counts are huge and logged feedback is sparse or biased.
method: meTS: mixed-effect Thompson sampling that shares statistical strength across actions.
dTS: diffusion-inspired priors to model dependencies among actions and reduce effective action complexity.
sDM and pessimistic policy-weighted objectives: latent-variable direct modeling plus concave, differentiable estimators to stabilize off-policy optimization.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical regret guarantees for on-policy methods and emphasizes that optimization error can dominate estimation error in large-action off-policy settings, with PAC-Bayesian control of bias-variance trade-offs.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality of structural assumptions and on careful optimization, since misspecification or unstable importance weights can still undermine off-policy estimates.
paper_title: On-Policy and Off-Policy Learning for Large Action Spaces
